Reference

User and administrator requirements

This page collects every requirement of the user and administrator documentation, one row for each id. Each requirement has a test. The ids are written [USR-nnn] where the page states the rule, and each row here links to that page.

Contract version: ilium:plugin@0.1.0. The platform is not implemented yet, so every row describes behaviour that the platform must have.

You will need

  • The Plugins for users page, for the words used here.
  • The Administration guide for the policy rows.

Id ranges

Range Subject Pages
USR-001 to USR-003 Overview promises Plugins for users
USR-010 to USR-014 Install and manage Install and manage plugins
USR-020 to USR-022, USR-080 to USR-088 Permissions in plain words Permissions explained
USR-030 to USR-033, USR-100, USR-101 Troubleshooting, safe mode, logs Troubleshooting plugins
USR-040 to USR-043 Core plugins Core plugins for users
USR-050 to USR-054 Extensions tab Extensions tab
USR-060 to USR-062, USR-102, USR-103 Privacy Plugin privacy
USR-070 to USR-073 Administration Administration guide
USR-110 FAQ Plugin FAQ
USR-120 to USR-129 Update, trust and keys Install and manage plugins, Packages
USR-130 Failure notice N14 Lifecycle
USR-140 to USR-143, USR-172 Uninstall and its effects Install and manage plugins, Lifecycle
USR-160 to USR-164 Recovery page and Plugins tab Settings screens, Settings plugin
USR-170, USR-171, USR-173 Install check order and update Security, Lifecycle
USR-200 to USR-209 Files on disk Plugin files
USR-210 to USR-220 Policy file and audit log Plugin policy

Requirements

Id Requirement Test Page
USR-001 The user documentation MUST state that all 30 core plugins ship with Ilium and need no install. search the page for the count 30 and the phrase "ship with Ilium". user-plugins-overview
USR-002 Ilium MUST NOT fetch, list, recommend or update plugins from the network on its own. run Ilium with all network traffic logged for one hour with two plugins installed and assert that no request is made for a plugin package or a plugin list. user-plugins-overview
USR-003 Ilium MUST show every grant a plugin requests before the plugin runs, and a grant the user does not give MUST stay locked. install a plugin that requests five grants, leave two unchecked, and assert that calls that need those two return not-permitted. user-plugins-overview
USR-010 Installing MUST NOT run any code of the package before the user has answered the permission review. install a package whose start function writes a file, decline the review, and assert that the file does not exist. user-install-and-manage
USR-011 A failed install MUST leave the installed plugins and their settings unchanged and MUST print one error that names the failed check. install a package with a bad file hash, list plugins before and after, and compare. user-install-and-manage
USR-012 The review dialog MUST list every requested permission, MUST start HIGH rows unchecked, and MUST record exactly the checked rows. install a package with three normal and two HIGH rows, accept the defaults, and assert that the grant file holds three granted and two declined entries. user-install-and-manage
USR-013 The plugin MUST be on after a successful install, unless the user chose to leave it off. install, then run ilium plugin list and assert the state. user-install-and-manage
USR-014 The first-start prompt MUST appear at most once per start, MUST NOT block other plugins, and after Not now MUST appear at most 3 more times in total. answer Not now at four consecutive starts and assert that the fifth start shows no prompt. user-install-and-manage
USR-020 A permission MUST apply to one plugin and one side, MUST be stored per user, and MUST NOT be shared through a project folder. grant a permission to the client side only, then call it from the server side and assert not-permitted. user-permissions-explained
USR-021 A plugin MUST NOT obtain a permission that its manifest does not list. call a host function whose permission is not in the manifest and assert that the call traps with host.capability-not-requested. user-permissions-explained
USR-022 The review dialog MUST start every HIGH row unchecked and every normal row checked. open the dialog for a package with both and assert the initial states. user-permissions-explained
USR-030 Safe mode MUST switch off every T2 and T3 plugin for the run, MUST leave core and bundled plugins on, and MUST NOT write the state to the registry. start in safe mode, stop, start normally and assert every plugin is as before. user-troubleshooting
USR-031 Safe mode MUST show a banner on every screen and MUST label every third-party row as off with the reason safe-mode. render the tree and the Plugins tab in safe mode. user-troubleshooting
USR-032 The recovery page MUST stay reachable when the Settings plugin is off or failed, and MUST NOT be replaceable by a plugin. turn off ilium.core.settings, open the recovery page, and re-enable it. user-troubleshooting
USR-033 Forget settings MUST delete only that plugin's settings values and MUST NOT delete permissions or data. set a value, forget, and compare the grant file and data folder. user-troubleshooting
USR-040 The Plugins tab and ilium plugin list MUST list all 30 core plugins with the tier T1, and MUST NOT offer to install or uninstall one. list plugins on a fresh profile, count 30 rows with ids ilium.core.*, and try ilium plugin uninstall ilium.core.tree, which must fail with plugin.not-removable. user-core-plugins
USR-041 The Plugins tab MUST refuse to turn off a core plugin marked "no" in the table, and MUST say why. press Space on ilium.core.tree and assert the refusal text. (Pending decision: the set of "no" plugins.) user-core-plugins
USR-042 A request to replace ilium.core.settings or ilium.core.sessions MUST fail at install with manifest.replaces-not-replaceable. install a package with such a replaces entry. user-core-plugins
USR-043 Ilium MUST ask the user to confirm every replaces entry at install, MUST allow at most 4 entries, and MUST NOT replace without a yes. install a package with 5 entries and assert the install is refused; with 1 entry assert the prompt and the choice Install without. user-core-plugins
USR-050 The Extensions tab MUST list contributors of each point in run order, MUST let the user move a contributor up or down, and the user's order MUST win over priority. set priorities 10 and 20, move the second above the first, call the point, and assert the new order. user-extensions-tab
USR-051 The host, not the plugin, MUST store the user's order and the toggles, and MUST keep them across restarts. reorder, restart, list. user-extensions-tab
USR-052 A hook that times out, traps or errors MUST count as "no change", and a timeout MUST NOT block or veto. let a veto handler sleep past its deadline and assert the action goes ahead. user-extensions-tab
USR-053 Three breaches in a row MUST stop the extension, MUST show a notice and a Reset button, and the stop MUST NOT be written to disk. cause three breaches, restart the contributor, and assert the extension is active again. user-extensions-tab
USR-054 An extension whose owner is missing or off MUST show "waiting for " and MUST become active when the owner returns. remove the owner, check the label, reinstall. user-extensions-tab
USR-060 Ilium MUST NOT send the list of installed plugins, plugin use, plugin logs or plugin errors to any remote party. run Ilium for one hour with five plugins and request logging, and assert that no request carries a plugin id. user-privacy
USR-061 A plugin MUST NOT read terminal text, history, agent prompts, transcripts, the clipboard, audio or location without the matching grant. for each item call the function without the grant and assert not-permitted. user-privacy
USR-062 Install, verify, update, uninstall and list MUST NOT use the network. run each in a network namespace without interfaces and assert success. user-privacy
USR-070 A policy MUST only restrict. No key of the policy MAY enable a plugin, grant or tier that Ilium refuses without a policy. set allowed_tiers = ["T3"] on Windows and assert that T3 is still refused. guide-administration
USR-071 A non-interactive install without --yes MUST fail with install.review-required, and --yes MUST NOT grant a HIGH permission that is not named. install a package with one HIGH row with --yes and assert that the row is declined. guide-administration
USR-072 An administrator MUST be able to block a running plugin by id, and the host MUST disable it at the next server start. add the id while the plugin runs, restart the server and assert the state Blocked by policy. guide-administration
USR-073 The documentation MUST state that the policy only restricts, where the file lives per system, and how to respond to a bad plugin. search this page for the three statements. guide-administration
USR-080 The Capabilities tab MUST show the plain wording, the grant string, the risk and the state (granted, declined, revoked) of every permission the plugin requests. open the tab for a plugin with ten requested grants and compare. user-permissions-explained
USR-081 A package that requests a bundled-only grant MUST fail to install with manifest.grant-tier. request plugins.manage in a T2 package. user-permissions-explained
USR-082 A grant string MUST be shown exactly as it will be matched, including its argument, so that the user can see the host, program or place. request http:api.example.com and assert the dialog shows that string. user-permissions-explained
USR-083 Ilium MUST ask the user before it opens a link from a plugin, for each target website and plugin, and MUST remember the answer. open two links to the same site and one to another site and count prompts: two. user-permissions-explained
USR-084 Ilium MUST NOT contact a host from a http:setting grant until the user has confirmed that host. set a new host in a setting, call, and assert no connection before the answer. user-permissions-explained
USR-085 A revoke MUST take effect for calls started after it, MUST make calls in flight return revoked, and MUST restart the plugin with the smaller set. start a long call, revoke, and assert revoked and a restart in the log. user-permissions-explained
USR-086 A HIGH grant MUST ask for confirmation in the attached client. run ilium plugin grants <id> --grant terminal.write with a client attached and assert the prompt. user-permissions-explained
USR-087 Ilium MUST show a footer indicator for 3 s after a plugin reads or writes the clipboard. read the clipboard from a test plugin and watch the footer. user-permissions-explained
USR-088 Ilium MUST drop toasts beyond 3 per 10 s per plugin and MUST end an input lock after 2 s. send ten toasts at once, count the visible ones; lock input and time the release. user-permissions-explained
USR-100 The plugin MUST restart after 1 s, then after 5 s, and MUST stay off at the third failure within 10 minutes. make a test plugin fail on start and measure. user-troubleshooting
USR-101 Turning a plugin on MUST clear its failure count. reach the stop, turn on, fail once, and assert a restart after 1 s. user-troubleshooting
USR-102 A T2 or T3 plugin MUST have no network access except through http: grants and the providers named above. from a test plugin, try a raw socket and a request to an ungranted host, and assert failure. user-privacy
USR-103 Ilium MUST refuse a request to a host that the plugin has no grant for, including a redirect target. redirect from a granted host to an ungranted host and assert not-permitted. user-privacy
USR-110 The documentation MUST answer, in this FAQ, whether a store exists, which systems run third-party plugins, what declining a permission does, and how to leave a bad plugin behind. search the page for each of the four answers. user-faq
USR-120 Ilium MUST show the full key fingerprint on request and the short form (first 4 and last 4 characters joined by an ellipsis) in the prompt, and MUST NOT trust a key without an explicit user answer. install a package signed by an unknown key and assert that the prompt appears and that declining installs nothing. user-install-and-manage
USR-121 Removing a trusted key MUST NOT remove, disable or change any installed plugin, and MUST mark plugins that it signed as untrusted in ilium plugin list. remove the key and list. user-install-and-manage
USR-122 An update of a T2 plugin MUST be signed by a trusted key. A key that signed the installed version MUST NOT be replaced silently by a different key. install version 1 signed by key A, then offer version 2 signed by unknown key B, and assert that the trust prompt appears and that the dialog names both fingerprints. user-install-and-manage
USR-123 An update MUST show only permissions that the installed version did not request, and MUST keep the answers already given. update from a package with two grants to one with three and assert one new row. user-install-and-manage
USR-124 A failed update MUST restore the previous version and its data and MUST show "Update failed, rolled back". update to a package whose activation fails and assert the version in ilium plugin list. user-install-and-manage
USR-125 Ilium MUST NOT check for, download or install updates by itself. with two plugins installed, run for one hour with request logging and assert that no update request is made. user-install-and-manage
USR-126 An update MUST keep the plugin id and MUST have a higher version. The signature MUST come from the key that signed the installed version, or from a key that the user trusts after seeing both fingerprints. offer an update signed by a second key and assert the prompt shows the old and the new fingerprint. packages
USR-127 Trust MUST be per key, MUST be stored in the user's trust list, and MUST NOT be created by installing a package without a prompt. install with a new key in a script without --yes and assert the install is refused. packages
USR-128 A T2 package whose key was removed from the trust list MUST keep running and MUST show untrusted in ilium plugin list. A later update MUST ask for trust again. remove the key, list, and offer an update. packages
USR-129 A publisher MUST keep the private key offline and MUST NOT put it in a package. A lost key means new packages need a new key and a new trust prompt. review ilium plugin keygen output for the path of the private key and its mode 0600. packages
USR-130 The notice N14 MUST read Plugin <name> stopped after 3 failures in 10 minutes: <export> <code or trap>. Turn it on again in Settings > Plugins. The <export> is the failing export. It names the view, as in views.render trap (sidebar), only when the failing export was views.render. The tree footer and the row in Settings > Plugins MUST show the same text. trap a plugin three times and compare the footer text and the row text with the template. lifecycle
USR-140 Uninstall MUST first mark the plugin as being removed, then stop it, then delete files, and after a crash the next start MUST finish the removal. kill the host after the mark and start again. user-install-and-manage
USR-141 Uninstall MUST NOT delete the data of any other plugin and MUST NOT remove trusted keys. compare the other plugins' folders before and after. user-install-and-manage
USR-142 A pane whose plugin is gone MUST stay in the tree with a placeholder and MUST come back to life when the plugin is installed again. remove, check the placeholder, reinstall, check the pane. user-install-and-manage
USR-143 Plugins that depend on the removed plugin MUST become dormant, not failed, and MUST wake up when it returns. remove the owner, check the state of the dependent plugin, reinstall the owner. user-install-and-manage
USR-160 The recovery page MUST offer the actions enable, disable, reset failures, uninstall, forget settings, safe mode and open config file, each with the key in the render, and MUST open from Ctrl+B then : when ilium.core.settings is off. turn the Settings plugin off, press the keys, and assert the page and each key. settings-screens
USR-161 The Plugins tab, ilium plugin list and the recovery page MUST use the row words of this table for the corresponding states, and MUST NOT introduce another word for the same state. put one plugin in each state and compare the words on the three surfaces. core-plugin-settings
USR-162 The Plugins tab MUST list every installed plugin including core plugins, with its tier badge and state. install two plugins, count the rows, and compare with ilium plugin list. core-plugin-settings
USR-163 The tab MUST offer Forget settings on a plugin's Details page. It MUST delete that plugin's saved settings values for the user and the open project, MUST ask for confirmation, and MUST NOT touch permissions or data. set a value, forget, assert the value is the default and the grant file is unchanged. core-plugin-settings
USR-164 The state words MUST be the same in the footer notice N14, which is defined in Lifecycle. stop a plugin and compare. core-plugin-settings
USR-170 Install, update and the Plugins screen MUST run the checks in the order of the table above, and MUST name the failing step's code in the error. build one package for each failing check, install each, and assert the code and that nothing is written to the store. security
USR-171 The error text for a refused install MUST begin Cannot install <name> <version>. and MUST name the check in plain words after it. assert the first line for a hash failure and for a tier failure. security
USR-172 An uninstall MUST apply the effects of the table above in the same host step that removes the plugin from the registry. remove a provider with a consumer, a contributor and a pane, and check each row. lifecycle
USR-173 An update MUST keep the grants the user already answered and MUST ask only for new ones. A failed update MUST roll back to the previous version. The user-facing rules are USR-123 and USR-124 in Install and manage plugins. update with one new grant and count the rows in the dialog. lifecycle
USR-200 The host MUST resolve <config>, <data> and <cache> with the directories crate for the project name ilium, and MUST NOT write plugin files anywhere else. start Ilium with XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME pointing at three empty folders, install a plugin, and assert that no plugin file appears outside those folders and the project's .ilium folder. reference-plugin-files
USR-201 The host MUST keep each item at the location in the table, and MUST create the parent folders on first use. on a clean profile, run install, grant, trust add, enable, disable and uninstall, then list the folders and match each file against the table. reference-plugin-files
USR-202 The host MUST write installed.json, the grant files and the trust store atomically: it writes a temporary sibling file, flushes it and renames it over the target. kill the process during a grant change and assert that the file holds either the old or the new content, never a mix. reference-plugin-files
USR-203 Grants MUST be stored per user and per plugin, and MUST NOT be stored in a project folder. grant fs.read:project while a project is open, open a second project and assert that the grant applies there and that <project>/.ilium/ holds no grant. reference-plugin-files
USR-204 The host MUST rotate the log at 1 MiB, MUST keep at most three rotated files, and MUST delete rotated files older than 14 days at server start. write 5 MiB of log lines through a test plugin and list the folder; then age <id>.log.2 by 15 days, restart, and assert it is gone. reference-plugin-files
USR-205 Each log line MUST have the four columns timestamp, level, plugin id and message, with the timestamp in the form YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss. read the log and match every line against the pattern. reference-plugin-files
USR-206 The host MUST create plugin folders with owner-only access and plugin files with owner-only read and write access. after an install, run stat on every created path and assert mode 0700 for folders and 0600 for files on Linux. reference-plugin-files
USR-207 The host MUST refuse to read a grant file or the trust store when another user can write to it, and MUST treat every third-party plugin as not allowed to run until the file is fixed. set the mode of a grant file to 0666, start Ilium, and assert that T2 and T3 plugins are refused at load with the code grants.unsafe-permissions while core plugins still run. reference-plugin-files
USR-208 A default uninstall MUST remove the package, the grants, the cache and the Extensions order entries, and MUST keep settings. install a plugin, write one setting, uninstall with no flag, and list what remains. reference-plugin-files
USR-209 --purge MUST also remove settings, data, storage buckets and the log, and --keep-data MUST keep data and storage without asking. The two flags exclude each other. run each flag on a copy of the same profile and compare the remains with the table. reference-plugin-files
USR-210 The host MUST read the policy file before it loads any third-party plugin, and MUST NOT load a third-party plugin when the file exists but cannot be read or parsed. make the file unreadable and start Ilium; assert that core plugins run and that every T2 and T3 plugin refuses to load with policy.invalid. reference-plugin-policy
USR-211 The host MUST ignore a system policy file that a non-administrator can write, MUST show a persistent notice, and MUST record the audit event policy-violation with the reason policy-file-writable ([SEC-182]). set the mode to 0666; assert the notice and the audit record. reference-plugin-policy
USR-212 The host MUST treat a policy with an unknown key or a wrong type as malformed and MUST name the line of the first error in the notice. write a policy with the key allow_thirdparty; assert that T2 and T3 plugins refuse to load, T1 plugins run, and the notice names line and key. reference-plugin-policy
USR-213 The host MUST read the policy at server start only. set packages.allow_third_party = false while a T2 plugin runs and assert that nothing changes; restart and assert the plugin is shown as Blocked by policy with the message policy.third-party-denied. reference-plugin-policy
USR-214 A grant that matches grants.deny MUST NOT be granted, MUST be shown as locked in the review dialog and in the Capabilities tab with the text "Blocked by your administrator", and MUST make calls return not-permitted. deny clipboard.read, install a plugin that requests it, and assert the row is locked and a call returns not-permitted with the message starting policy: and the log line refused clipboard.read by <function> (policy). reference-plugin-policy
USR-215 A plugin whose manifest requests a denied grant MUST still install and run, with that grant refused. install such a plugin and assert state enabled and the refusal log line. reference-plugin-policy
USR-216 plugins.deny_ids MUST win over plugins.allow_ids. list one id in both and assert it cannot be installed, with the code policy.blocked and the message starting policy.id-denied:. reference-plugin-policy
USR-217 The host MUST check the policy keys in the order above and report the first failing key as the detail code. write a policy that fails four keys at once and assert the detail code is the first in the order. reference-plugin-policy
USR-218 The policy MUST NOT stop a core plugin or a bundled T1 plugin from running. set packages.allow_third_party = false and packages.allowed_tiers = []; assert all 30 core plugins still start. reference-plugin-policy
USR-219 The host MUST write a policy-loaded audit record at start when a policy file exists, and a policy-violation record when a plugin or file violates it, and MUST NOT write plugin data into either. start with a policy that denies one installed plugin and count the two records. reference-plugin-policy
USR-220 The host MUST delete rotated audit files older than audit.keep_days at server start ([SEC-224]). age a rotated file by 366 days and restart. reference-plugin-policy

Pending decisions

These rows are proposals. The manual states them so a test can be written, and the owner of the platform must confirm or change them before release.

Subject Proposal in this manual Where
Safe mode Third-party plugins are off for one run and nothing is written to installed.json ([LIF-004]). Troubleshooting plugins
Administrator policy file A TOML file in a system folder that only restricts. Plugin policy
Audit log Always on, with rotation and retention set by audit.max_mib and audit.keep_days. Plugin policy
Which core plugins a user can turn off The "can you turn it off" column of the core plugin tables. Core plugins for users
Data choice at uninstall The dialog asks keep or purge. The default without a terminal is keep. Install and manage plugins
Update asks again Only new permissions appear in the dialog. Install and manage plugins
Check order The table of check order against the 12-step pipeline. Security
Row state words One table of state words for the tab, the CLI and the recovery page. Settings plugin
